newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on harvest concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on harvest concerns.

text.p: Concerns that wet weather in the U.S. Midwest will delay corn harvest and slow the maturity pace of the crop boosted CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The midday reports showed even more moisture than the morning reports so it took off from there," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Meteorologists early Wednesday said widespread rain was forecast for the U.S. central Plains and Midwest for the balance of the week, which should delay corn harvest.
But traders said there were two sides to that story.
"There is a divergence in the models (computer weather models). The American model is dry and the European is wet," Cermak said.

Weather Services Corp Wednesday said the four to five day outlook continues in disagreement with the U.S. model moving cooler and drier air into the Midwest over the weekend but the European model shows the weather pattern unsettled which would prevent any damaging cold weather from occuring.
Corn futures closed two cents per bushel higher to one cent lower, with December up 1-3/4 at $3.12-1/4. March was up two at $3.19.
Technicians early Wednesday cited initial resistance in the December at $3.11-3/4 and the second level of resistance was at $3.14 and first support at $3.09-1/2.
Rosenthal Collins bought seven million bushels of December and bought 6.5 million March, the traders said. E.D. and F. Man International bought two million December, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 39,000, down from 50,871 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

Active dealings were noted in corn options with Goldenberg Hehmeyer buying 2,000 March $3.00 puts at 7-7-1/4 cents and Rand Financial bought 500 March $2.60 puts at 3/4 cents, the traders said. LIT America bought 600 December $3.80 calls at 1/2 cent and Term Commodities bought 200 December $3.60 calls and sold 400 December $3.80 calls at even money, they said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 19,804 Tuesday.
